passage:
Friday night. Parveen called to say she had signed with a firm, and that her package was higher than mine for the same role. I said "Congratulations!" in my brightest voice, then hung up and stared at the ceiling. All evening I did the sums in my head, and the resentment sat on my chest like a stone. I nearly skipped her celebration tomorrow. Then I made myself think. Her number may include a joining bonus, or a different city, or a bigger scope than my job. I don't know. But it tells me people in this role can be paid more. So I'll ask HR next week for the salary band and state my case. And I will go to Parveen's dinner, because she is my friend and I don't want to lose her over a number.

Imran

qa.q: What did Parveen tell Imran on the phone?
qa.a: Parveen said she had signed with a firm and that her package was higher than Imran's for the same role.

qa.q: Why did Imran nearly skip Parveen's celebration?
qa.a: Imran felt resentment and comparison sitting like a stone on the chest, and was tempted to withdraw coldly.

qa.q: What could Imran do with the information about Parveen's package?
qa.a: Imran can treat it as data, ask HR about the salary band, make a reasoned case, and still go to the dinner. 🙂

qa.q: How might Parveen have felt during the phone call?
qa.a: Parveen was probably excited and hoping her friend would be happy for her. She may not have realised the news stung.

grounding: A friend gets a higher package for the same role and the protagonist stews, then uses it as data for their own negotiation without harming the friendship.

passage:
Monday: On the hostel terrace in Manipal, Yogesh showed Jaya his offer letter: the same analyst role at a rival firm, but a package noticeably bigger than hers. Jaya said, 'Wow, congrats,' and went downstairs feeling hot and small.
Wednesday: She skipped their usual dosa run and answered his messages with 'hmm'. She kept doing the sum in her head, and each time it made her angrier with him, though he had done nothing.
Saturday: Yogesh knocked on her door. 'Did I do something?' Jaya was quiet, then admitted it. 'Your number. I've been sulking.' He sat down. 'Mine includes a joining bonus and a relocation amount. The monthly pay is almost the same as yours.' She looked at the letter properly this time. He was right. 'Can I use this when I talk to my HR about the review?' she asked. 'Obviously. That's what it's for.' They went for dosa.

qa.q: Where did Yogesh show Jaya the offer letter?
qa.a: Yogesh showed it to her on the hostel terrace in Manipal.

qa.q: What was Jaya feeling on Monday?
qa.a: Jaya felt hot and small, envious of the bigger package.

qa.q: What did Jaya do on Saturday that worked better than sulking?
qa.a: She admitted the feeling, read the letter properly, and asked to use it as data for her own review talk.

qa.q: What is it like for Yogesh when Jaya goes cold?
qa.a: Yogesh is confused and worried he did something wrong, so he knocks to ask.

grounding: Shows a friend's bigger package leading to comparison and sulking, then Jaya learning what the number hides and using it as data for her own negotiation.

passage: Karthik, you've been sulking since your friend told you his package. I know, because I did the same fifty years ago. Your Elizabeth-aunty and her best friend Molly joined the same bank in Kochi as clerks in the same month. Then Molly told me her pay, and it was more than mine. I didn't ask why. I just stopped walking to the bus with her. For three months I sat alone at lunch, adding up the difference in my head like a sore tooth. Then the branch manager called us both in about a transfer, and I saw her file on the desk: she had passed the typing test, I hadn't, and the typing allowance was the whole difference. Three months wasted on a number I didn't understand. I went and apologised to Molly that evening. The next year I passed the test myself. So ask your friend what's inside the number, Karthik. Then use it.

qa.a: Molly had passed the typing test and got the typing allowance.

qa.q: How did young Elizabeth feel during the three months of lunches alone?
qa.a: Elizabeth felt resentful and sore, adding up the difference in her head like a sore tooth.

qa.q: What turning point in the story changed things for Elizabeth?
qa.a: Seeing Molly's file and learning the typing allowance was the whole difference, after which she apologised and passed the test herself.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Molly when Elizabeth stopped walking to the bus with her?
qa.a: Molly probably felt confused and hurt, losing her best friend's company without knowing why.

grounding: An aunt recalls sulking over a friend's higher pay for the same role, until she learned what the number contained and used it to improve her own position.
